question.text: Under a Right of First Offer (ROFO), if a selling shareholder receives a LOWER third-party offer than the ROFO-holder's prior offer, the selling shareholder must:

answer.text: Retain the shares — no sale is permitted
Sell at the lower market offer, having exhausted the ROFO-holder's right
Compulsorily sell to the ROFO-holder at the ROFO-holder's previously quoted offer price

explanation.text: The Logic: Under ROFO, the holder gives its best quote FIRST. Then the seller tests the market. If the market offer is LOWER than the ROFO-holder's offer, the selling shareholder must offer (and sell) the shares to the ROFO-holder at the holder's offered price. The Trap: Selling at the lower market price ignores the holder's right. Retaining shares ignores the mechanism. Renegotiation upward is not the ROFO consequence. Note: The workbook directly supports the ROFO mechanics: if the market offer is lower, the selling shareholder must offer the shares to the ROFO holder at the holder's previously offered price. Founder-friendly/ROFR negotiating commentary has been removed as not source-supported.
